title: Google Pledges $5 Million to IIT Kharagpur for Advanced AI Research, Education and Campus Technology

Google has announced $5 million in funding for the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur to accelerate advanced artificial intelligence research, expand AI education and strengthen the institute's technological infrastructure.
The announcement was made on November 21, 2026, during IIT Kharagpur's Platinum Jubilee celebrations.
Google CEO Sundar Pichai, an alumnus of the institute, played a key role in facilitating the funding, according to IIT Kharagpur Director Suman Chakraborty.
Issue/Event: Google announces $5 million funding commitment to accelerate AI research and technology education.
Authority/Organisation: Google and Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur.

Action Taken: Funding announced for advanced AI research, AI training and campus-level technology development.
- Impact: The initiative aims to strengthen India's AI research ecosystem and develop the next generation of scientific and technical talent.
The funding is designed to support researchers and students through three major areas: advanced AI research, educational opportunities and AI capacity building across the campus.
Under the research component, IIT Kharagpur will focus on applying artificial intelligence to Indic languages, materials science, agriculture and educational technology.
These areas have potential applications in language accessibility, scientific research, agricultural innovation and digital learning.
The initiative is expected to support research teams working on practical AI solutions for challenges relevant to India.
However, Google has not yet announced the individual projects, research teams or specific funding allocations under each area.
Artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly important in sectors such as agriculture, education, scientific research, healthcare and language technology.
The funding could help IIT Kharagpur expand its research capabilities and develop AI applications addressing challenges specific to India.

Research into Indic languages is particularly relevant because language accessibility remains an important factor in bringing digital services and information to people across different linguistic communities.
Similarly, AI applications in agriculture and educational technology could support new approaches to agricultural research, learning and knowledge access.
The initiative also highlights the growing role of partnerships between global technology companies and Indian academic institutions in developing advanced technological capabilities.
The second component focuses on expanding AI education and training.
The funding will support curriculum development and learning opportunities for students, faculty members and teachers.
This initiative is intended to strengthen technical skills and improve access to AI-related knowledge within the academic community.
It also reflects the growing importance of artificial intelligence across education, research and professional development.
The third component will focus on strengthening IIT Kharagpur's AI infrastructure.
Google said the funding would support the development of AI frameworks and tools to improve the institute's technological ecosystem.
The announcement comes as Indian educational institutions increasingly seek to expand their capabilities in artificial intelligence, machine learning and advanced computing.
Sundar Pichai said the collaboration would help accelerate IIT Kharagpur's work in areas such as Indic languages, agriculture and education.
He also highlighted the importance of ensuring that the benefits of AI reach people across India.
Separately, IIT Kharagpur Director Suman Chakraborty also announced that alumnus Jyoti Chatterjee had pledged another $5 million as a seed endowment for a next-generation data initiative.
This is a separate contribution and should not be confused with Google's funding commitment.
The Google funding represents a significant institutional commitment towards AI research and education.
Its eventual impact will depend on how the institute translates the broad funding priorities into research projects, training programmes and practical technology applications.
The next stage will involve translating the funding commitment into specific research and educational programmes.
The institute's future announcements will help clarify how the funding is distributed and what practical outcomes emerge from the collaboration.
